summary: 66-foot UW forestry tower built 1929 near Eatonville, WA; used by the AWS in 1942, abandoned around 1950 and removed. Four footings remain near the high point.

facts.design: 66-foot steel tower with 7-by-7-foot cab, built 1929; ground living quarters cabin
facts.status_note: Tower removed in the 1950s. Willhite describes four tower footings near the high point.

access.note: UW says Pack Forest is open to hikers. Its site posts notices of temporary recreational closures for active logging.

visit.trail_note: Reached by roads or a mix of roads and trails. A short side trail from the road leads to the highest spot and a memorial rock.

events.note: 66-foot steel tower with 7-by-7 cab built by the UW College of Forestry to guard Pack Forest; a ground living quarters cabin was also on the site
1934 panoramic photos taken from the tower
USGS placed a monument at the site called PACK
AWS used the tower to spot airplanes during the war; photo captions show AWS observers and a setup in January 1942
AWS use was discontinued by April 1942 because other sites gave good coverage; no longer in use by May 2
Firelookout.com gives 1950; Willhite says abandoned sometime in the 1950s
Register says the tower was removed in the 1950s
Registered September 13, 2010; nominated by Irene Potter

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com says two miles south of Eatonville; a 2012 blog post says two miles east. The story reports both.
Willhite says it is not known where the lookout ended up; a reader comment on the 2012 blog says it was taken apart and moved to a ranch in Alder. The story reports both as claims.
Firelookout.com gives 1950; Willhite says sometime in the 1950s; the register says removed in the 1950s. These agree at different precision.

sources.title: Pack Forest Highpoint - Lookout Mountain - Hugo Peak

notes_for_editor: Brief status gone, the 1929 build date, the 2010 registration and the coordinates all match the sources, so no corrections. Sources give three names for the high point (Pack Forest Highpoint, Lookout Mountain, Hugo Peak). The footings come from Willhite's text and photo captions; not verified on site. Reader comments on the 2012 blog are personal recollections and left unweighted. One commenter says they climbed the tower in the late 1960s or early 1970s, which conflicts with the 1950 abandonment date; left out as unreliable. UW's notice about temporary closures should be checked before any visit advice.
